newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF may require identification in Eurobond tax law.
newsitem.headline: MOF may require identification in Eurobond tax law.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) may retain a rule which exempts foreigners from paying a withholding tax on income gains from investments in Eurobonds, but on the condition that buyers identify themselves, industry sources said on Friday.
MOF, the Trade Ministry, Japanese issuers and the financial industry have been debating the issue since early October.
Many have opposed MOF's idea to require identification, saying for instance, it could cause problems for foreigners who want to buy Eurobonds, including Euroyen bonds, issued by Japanese borrowers.
The industry and the Trade Ministry have been calling for the special tax exemption law to be kept. It is normally reviewed every two years.
"MOF is expected to attach a scheme that would require identification of investors," a brokerage source said.
"We want to see the details, but MOF is expected to keep it secret until the very last moment to avoid massive opposition," the source said.
They expect the scheme to be formally announced on Tuesday, when MOF submits the plan to the Liberal Democratic Party's tax panel for discussion.

MOF wants to close a loophole which gives a tax break on Euroyen purchases to Japanese investors who buy the bonds through their overseas subsidiaries. The official said that MOF did not intend to impose a tax on foreigners.
"We are working as hard as possible to come up with a decent rule, but we are not thinking of keeping the present law like it is," the official at MOF's Tax Affairs Division said.
"We have been asking for counter-proposals, but unfortunately we have not seen a decent proposal."
